references.text: Moses stretches out his hand over the sea as the Lord commands, and the Israelites cross on dry ground—the direct fulfillment of the command to move forward.
Moses cries out to the Lord again in a crisis situation, showing a pattern of prayer in times of distress.
The Lord gives the command for when the Israelites should break camp and move forward; the same Hebrew root נסע (nasa) is used.
The Lord asks Joshua why he is lying face down and commands him to act—a parallel situation where prayer must be followed by action.
The Lord tells Nehemiah that it is time for action, not just mourning—a similar theme that there is a time to act.
Isaiah refers to the Lord's way through the sea and his power over the great waters—a direct reference to the event at the Red Sea.
A prophetic reference to the one who dried up the sea and made the depths of the ocean a path for the redeemed to cross.
By faith they passed through the Red Sea as on dry land—the New Testament confirms that Israel's obedience to move forward was an act of faith.
